Package org.geysermc.paletter.item

Class ItemRegistry

java.lang.Object
org.geysermc.paletter.item.ItemRegistry
All Implemented Interfaces:
org.cloudburstmc.protocol.common.DefinitionRegistry<org.cloudburstmc.protocol.bedrock.data.definitions.ItemDefinition>
public final class ItemRegistry extends Object implements org.cloudburstmc.protocol.common.DefinitionRegistry<org.cloudburstmc.protocol.bedrock.data.definitions.ItemDefinition>
The compiled item palette of one Palette. It is the item DefinitionRegistry for the codec, and answers both directions of item translation:
  • item(int) / resolve(ItemVariant): what to send for a canonical id or a variant (written against the newest Bedrock version);
  • match(ItemData): which canonical id a stack the client sent is;
  • encode(org.geysermc.paletter.item.BedrockItemStack) and decode(org.cloudburstmc.protocol.bedrock.data.inventory.ItemData): whole stacks, see Palette.
It also knows which block each block item is sent with, so consumers never have to work that out from the creative inventory themselves.
Since:
1.0.0

    • blockOf

      public @Nullable RegisteredBlockState blockOf(@NonNull BedrockItemVariant variant)
      The block an item variant is sent with in this version: the single owner of that decision. For an item that places blocks, a block state of the variant wins (adapted to this version), otherwise the item's block, which is decided in this order:
      1. an override of a layer (PaletteLayer.Builder#blockItem);
      2. the bundled block to item relation of the data (VanillaData#blockItems): the block whose first creative stack the item has, else the block named like the item, else the first block that places it (sorted by identifier), in its default state;
      3. a block state of the item's creative stacks (items the relation does not know);
      4. for data without the relation: a block named like the item, in its default state;
      5. the block of a custom block item.
      Parameters:
      variant - a variant, written against the newest Bedrock version like resolve(ItemVariant)
      Returns:
      the block, or null if the item is not a block item here (or does not exist and has no fallback)
      Since:
      1.0.0

    • fallbackOf

      public @Nullable BedrockItemVariant fallbackOf(@NonNull BedrockItemVariant variant)
      What this version sends instead of a variant: its fallback, that is the replacement of a ItemFallback (also a forced one), or the default fallback (minecraft:unknown) for a variant the version lacks. A lookup in the canonical table, cheap enough to ask for every item at startup (unlike Palette#explain).
      Parameters:
      variant - a variant, written against the newest Bedrock version
      Returns:
      the variant that is sent in its place (the aux of the fallback's variant, else the aux of the replaced item), or null if the variant is sent as itself, or nothing is sent for it at all (see isFallback(org.geysermc.paletter.vanilla.BedrockItemVariant))
      Since:
      1.0.0

    • match

      @Internal public int match(@NonNull org.cloudburstmc.protocol.bedrock.data.inventory.ItemData data)
      Identifies a stack the client sent: its runtime id is looked up in a hash table, then the few variants of that item are told apart by damage. Does not allocate.

      Order: a variant with this damage, then the item's base variant. A variant that only reached this version through a fallback never shadows the item's own variants, and never serves as a base variant. A stack that exists here only as the fallback of several canonical ids (e.g. the shared minecraft:unknown of the default fallback) is not matched: any of them would be an arbitrary claim. A fallback reached by exactly one canonical id still matches it.

      Returns:
      the canonical id, or -1 for air, an unknown definition, an item that is no variant of the newest version, or a stack shared by the fallbacks of several canonical ids
